title: The Watson cousins and the Jackson family of musicians
summary: He lists Charlie, Eddie and Henry Watson and the Jackson family who played with his father.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Fiddlers and reading violinists of New Orleans

blocks.x: What about those Watsons? You said there was Charlie Watson played drums. They was, uh, Charlie Blue. They was Edward Watson. They had Harry Watson.

And they had, uh, Eddie, Harry, and, uh, oh, nah, I can't think of his name. They used to call his nickname, uh, oh, Eddie, Harry, I think his name. And they had Charlie. Charlie Watson. But he used to call him Charlie Blue Weller. Eddie played, uh, guitar for a long time. Then he ended up playing fire. For a while he didn't play too long. And the, uh, the one I was trying to call his name, the name was Henry Watson. And, uh, well they played for a long time. What did Henry play? Henry played, uh, banjo.
Were these cousins or brothers or wasons?
Cousins. Cousins. All those Watsons was cousins. Cousins of his?
Of their? Cousins of ours. Yeah. And were they brothers, all of them? All of those were brothers like we were. I mean like we are.

Yeah. Now they had, uh, oh, they had, uh, uh, Jackson used to play bass with my daddy too. Mm-hmm. Yeah. He used to play, well Jackson used to play bass with my daddy. And, uh, we had a daughter, Anita Jackson, she played piano. And, uh, now she has a brother, she passed, and she has a brother, his name is Joseph Jackson, where he plays piano. He still plays.
Oh, and music hits a family, it really hits a family, doesn't it?
